checks.label: If the product of two numbers is zero then one or both of the numbers must be zero: on every screen set equal to 0, at every pointer setting the product bar reads 0 exactly where a bracket bar reads 0, and only there does the dot sit on the axis
The graph of a quadratic function is a U-shaped curve called a parabola: every screen's curve falls to one lowest point and rises again on both sides of it, and is drawn whole once shown
Each picture draws its question's own equation: at every x from −30 to 30 in steps of 0.5, the brackets' product equals the value it is set to exactly when the question holds
Every puzzle accepts only its right answer: the right one names every root of its equation and nothing else, and each wrong one puts back a value that fails the equation or misses a root

The worked numbers: at x = 3 the bars read 1 and −2 and the product −2, the ends of screen 1 make 18, = 10 holds at x = 0 and x = 7 but x = 12 makes 70, the wrong picks make 28, 40, 28, 10, 66, −4, 768, 8, 220 and 52, and every line of working adds up

Before Check a puzzle draws no curve and its pointer sits off every root; after a right answer the curve is drawn whole and the pointer ends on the last root, where the dot meets the line its product is set equal to

Set equal to 10, the dot meets the dashed line at x = 0 and x = 7, where the brackets read −2 and −5, then 5 and 2, so neither is 10; with both brackets x − 3 the bars reach zero together at x = 3 only and the curve never goes below the axis
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2.5 s
